answer: Collateral is slashed jointly when correlated behavioural faults fire inside the same window. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The lagoon is the collateral at risk, the velvet the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the canyon the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many velvet groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the lagoon into smaller, individually useless stakes.
